newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Orange debut yr focus on sign-ups.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Orange debut yr focus on sign-ups.

text.p: British mobile telephone company Orange Plc should see widening losses when it reports its first annual results since flotation on March 11.
But, in a relatively new market which needs upfront investment, attention is likely to focus on revenues and signs of customer loyalty, analysts said.
"We will be watching what is happening with average subscriber revenues and levels of churn (the number of customers dropping out)," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Pretax losses are expected to be between 237 million and 223.3 million stg compared with 140.5 million stg a year ago. Loss per share is expected to be between 21.3 pence and 19 pence compared with 18 pence last time.
Orange, which floated just over a year ago at 205 pence per share, said in January that subscribers had doubled to over 785,000 in 1996.
That gave the company, partly owned by Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa and British Aerospace, an 11.5 percent of the UK market for mobile phones, against seven percent at the end of 1995.
Shares were trading at 212-1/2 pence at 1340 GMT, up half a penny.
Orange said in January that its churn rate of 18.6 percent was around a third lower than the industry average.
"Orange has an exceptionally good record on churn, it is much more careful than competitors at choosing customers and they tend to stay," the analyst said.
Orange's major competitors in mobile telephones include market leader Vodafone Group and Cellnet, 60-percent owned by British Telecommunications.
Orange is not expected to move into profits until 1998 or 1999, but analysts said a strong set of debut year results could prompt expectations to be accelerated.
